children: By Staff Writer

The Federal Government, on Wednesday, commissioned a 3MW captive solar hybrid power project at the University of Abuja (now Yakubu Gowon University), strengthening electricity supply for teaching, research, laboratories, digital services and other critical university operations.

The project was part of the Phase II Energising Education Programme (EEP) with support from the World Bank, with utility-scale hybrid solar power plants being developed in seven federal universities and two affiliated teaching hospitals across the country.
Commissioning the facility, the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, said the investment demonstrated the practical connection between Nigeria’s energy transition and human capital development.
According to Tegbe, the facility would provide a more reliable energy base for teaching and research, saying its long-term performance would be the real measure of the investment.

He said, “There is perhaps no better place to demonstrate the practical value of Nigeria’s energy transition than a university. A university brings together everything that a modern energy system is expected to support: learning, research, healthcare, technology, administration and, increasingly, the digital infrastructure through which knowledge is created and shared. The commissioning is not the conclusion of the investment. It is the beginning of its most important phase.”

Managing Director/CEO of REA, Abba Aliyu, said the EEP had grown beyond providing electricity infrastructure to demonstrating how energy investment can support education and human capital development.

Aliyu said REA’s experience implementing projects at this scale had also reinforced the importance of planning for the entire life of an energy asset, from construction and commissioning to operation, maintenance and long-term performance.

While pledging REA’s continued efforts to develop models that attract private capital, expand electricity access and protect public investment, Aliyu said renewable energy infrastructure has been delivered to 22 federal universities and three affiliated teaching hospitals, with more than 100MW of clean energy deployed and over 600,000 students and 50,000 academic and administrative staff impacted nationwide.

“When the Energizing Education Programme was conceived, the ambition was straightforward: to change what reliable electricity could mean for Nigeria’s public universities. Not simply to put solar panels on campuses, but to create the conditions for students to learn, lecturers to teach, researchers to work, laboratories to function and universities to operate with greater certainty.

“We have become very good at asking, ‘How do we build more?’ We must now become equally rigorous about asking, ‘How do we protect what we have already built? How do we make it perform? And how do we preserve its value?” the REA boss said.

Chairman of the Senate Committee on Power, Senator Enyinnaya Abaribe, said the project demonstrated the connection between energy policy, effective implementation and tangible improvements in the lives of Nigerians.

He said the legislature would continue to provide the legislative environment and oversight required to support power-sector investment, strengthen accountability and ensure that projects deliver sustainable benefits.

“Sustainability must therefore remain a priority,” Abaribe said, stressing the importance of university ownership and appropriate arrangements for the operation, maintenance and protection of the facility throughout its useful life, the lawmaker said.
In his remarks, the Vice Chancellor of the university, Professor Hakeem Babatunde Fawehinmi, described the project as an investment in the university’s academic mission.

“A university such as ours cannot teach effectively, conduct meaningful research, operate its laboratories, sustain digital services or even provide the conducive environment required for learning and innovation without dependable power supply,” Fawehinmi said.

Apart from the University of Abuja, other beneficiaries of the EEP Phase II project are the Nigeria Defence Academy (NDA), Kaduna State, with 2.5MW; University of Maiduguri and Teaching Hospital, Borno State, 12MW; Federal University of Gashua, Yobe State, 1.5MW; University of Calabar, Cross River State, 7MW; Michael Okpara University of Agriculture, Abia State, 3MW; and the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, Ogun State, 3MW.

Beyond electricity supply, the project included a Renewable Energy Workshop and Training Centre to support practical learning and skills development in renewable energy technologies, and also incorporated a female STEM component that provides students with practical exposure to renewable energy and opportunities within the sector.
The project was delivered through collaboration between the Federal Government and the REA, the Nigeria Electrification Project, the World Bank, the university and EMONE Energy Solutions.
